issues: legalForce says the icons were 'never finalised'. That is overstated. The cited beta page says only 'They are not yet final.' (June 2011), and no source read shows the project's final state. A later Mozilla wiki draft, 'Privacy Icons v0.2' (Aug-Sep 2011), shows the project still active and refocused on the web-app store, add-ons and mobile apps.

The year needs context. 2011 is the date of the beta page, but the Mozilla project began earlier. The 'Drumbeat/Challenges/Privacy Icons' wiki page was created on 12 Nov 2009 (MediaWiki revision history, first edit by David Eaves), and Aza Raskin's alpha post refers to a Mozilla privacy workshop held 'earlier this year'. The alpha's exact date is still unconfirmed: the archived post has no date. Keep year 2011 as the record's documented convention, but the note should not imply the idea began in 2011.

body 'Mozilla-convened working groups' is acceptable. The beta page says the icons 'are the result of a number of working groups convened by Aza Raskin' (then at Mozilla; 'Owner: Ben Moskowitz, Mozilla; Aza Raskin (initiator)'), and Raskin's post says 'Mozilla convened a privacy workshop'.

fieldFixes.legalForce: Intended as legal declarations "bolted on" to a site's privacy policy; the beta set was "not yet final" (June 2011) and no final, binding set was found in sources read
fieldFixes.fate: An alpha set (Aza Raskin, c. 2010), a beta set (Mozilla wiki, updated 28 June 2011, "not yet final") and a v0.2 draft (Aug-Sep 2011) refocused on the web-app store, add-ons and mobile apps; machine readability promised "soon"; no final set or adoption figures found in sources read.
fieldFixes.note: Year = the dated beta page (2011). The Mozilla project is older: a Drumbeat 'Privacy Icons' challenge page was created on the Mozilla wiki on 12 November 2009, and the alpha followed a Mozilla privacy workshop (alpha commonly dated 2010; not confirmed in a dated primary source). Modelled explicitly on Creative Commons, as MyTerms is, but proffered by the site, not the person.
